meta.title: The World Before Bitcoin — 2-Minute Cut
meta.hook: In August 1971, Britain asked America for its gold. The gold wasn't there.
meta.description:
A fast-paced 2-minute cut of Episode 1: The World Before Bitcoin. 1971-2008: the gold standard breaks, inflation and bank failures follow, and a small group of cryptographers keep trying to build money no one can switch off.

Educational history and commentary. Not financial advice.

scenes.narration: September fifteenth, one forty-five in the morning: Lehman Brothers filed for bankruptcy.
scenes.visual_objective: Staff carrying boxes out of 745 Seventh Avenue in the dark

scenes.narration: Six hundred and thirty-nine billion dollars in assets. The largest bankruptcy in American history.
scenes.visual_objective: The figure counting up, then the record label landing under it

scenes.narration: Twenty-four hours later, the Federal Reserve lent eighty-five billion dollars to a single insurance company.
scenes.visual_objective: The AIG facility as one hero figure against the days around it

scenes.narration: On the third of October, Congress authorised seven hundred billion dollars to buy the bad debt.
scenes.visual_objective: The three rescues stacked so the scale reads instantly

scenes.narration: And on the streets, the other half of the story.
scenes.visual_objective: Real footage: a residential street of ordinary American houses, seen at ground level

scenes.narration: In the decade that followed, almost eight million American homes were lost to foreclosure.
scenes.visual_objective: Completed foreclosures counting up past eight million and holding

scenes.narration: Not bailed out. Not rescued. Foreclosed.
scenes.visual_objective: Recreation: a foreclosure notice taped to the inside of a suburban front window

scenes.narration: The institutions that built the crisis were handed public money.
scenes.visual_objective: Real footage looking up the glass face of a banking tower — the money went up there

scenes.narration: The people who trusted them were handed eviction notices.
scenes.visual_objective: Real footage: a foreclosure / repossession sign staked on a front lawn

scenes.narration: Something broke that autumn that was bigger than any bank.
scenes.visual_objective: Recreation: a wide, emptied trading floor at night, screens dark, chairs pushed back

scenes.narration: For thirty-seven years the world had run on a single sentence. Trust us.
scenes.visual_objective: The two words that carried the entire system since 1971

scenes.narration: In the autumn of two thousand and eight, hundreds of millions of people stopped.
scenes.visual_objective: The two words from the card before breaking apart and falling out of the bottom of frame

scenes.narration: And while the world was collapsing —
scenes.visual_objective: Recreation: a city at night seen from far above, half the windows dark

scenes.narration: while governments printed, and banks failed, and families were carried out of their houses —
scenes.visual_objective: Recreation: three fragments in one held frame — a press, a shuttered branch, a packed car

scenes.narration: somewhere, in a room nobody has ever found,
scenes.visual_objective: Recreation: an anonymous desk, one monitor's glow, the chair empty

scenes.narration: someone was quietly writing a nine-page document
scenes.visual_objective: Nine blank pages fanning open, none of them legible

scenes.narration: that would change money forever.
scenes.visual_objective: The final line landing, then black

scenes.narration: Episode two. The nine pages.
